# FastAPI Development

Implement the requested FastAPI behavior using the project's supported versions, established stack and public contract. Preserve unrelated work. Return implemented changes, observed verification and remaining limits.

## Route precisely

- Use for creating or changing FastAPI endpoints, Pydantic request/response boundaries, dependencies, lifespan resources or streaming behavior.
- Use `code-review` for a read-only review of an existing diff. Do not start implementation merely because reviewed code uses FastAPI.
- Use `api-and-interface-design` for a proposed API contract, `review-spec` for a proposed specification and `verify-impl` for conformance to an accepted spec.
- Use `uv-project-workflow` when the requested result is Python environment or dependency management; the presence of a Python file does not choose uv.
- Do not activate for unrelated Python, Django, Flask, generic asyncio, or an API with no FastAPI requirement. Establish the framework if it is genuinely unresolved.

## Establish the contract and compatibility

1. Read repository instructions and working-tree state. Identify the owning app/package, affected routes and tests; preserve dirty overlapping work.
2. Read Python constraints, manifests/lockfiles, resolved FastAPI/Starlette/Pydantic versions, ASGI deployment, lifespan and test configuration. Distinguish a released installed API from upstream main.
3. State the requested inputs, outputs, status/error behavior, authorization, compatibility and resource ownership. For streams, name the protocol and whether incremental delivery or disconnect behavior is required.
4. Consult [references/contracts-and-versions.md](references/contracts-and-versions.md) only for the affected features. Verify a feature against the installed version's signatures/source or matching official docs before using it. If evidence is unavailable, use an established supported path or state the missing verification; do not invent a version floor or upgrade automatically.

## Implement the smallest coherent change

- Prefer `Annotated` parameter/dependency declarations for new compatible code. Reuse dependency aliases when useful; avoid unrelated rewrites of working signatures.
- Define validation where untrusted values enter. Keep missing values, `None`, defaults, coercion and strictness consistent with the contract. For new required Pydantic fields prefer no ellipsis default; do not treat existing `RootModel` or ellipsis as globally deprecated.
- Declare the public output schema through a supported return type or `response_model`. Keep internal secrets out of that schema. Direct `Response` objects need their own serialization/filtering guarantees.
- Keep router/app dependencies and authorization explicit. Use ordinary validation instead of dependency machinery when no external state or shared execution is needed.
- Match sync/async execution to actual calls. Keep blocking work off the event loop with a supported, bounded approach; preserve the chosen DB/HTTP libraries unless replacement is requested or demonstrably necessary.
- Own each session, client, file, task and generator until its last consumer finishes. Align `yield` cleanup with response consumption and the installed dependency-scope semantics. Do not capture request resources for detached work without a lifecycle and failure owner.
- Use the requested stream protocol. Check support before adopting native SSE, JSON Lines helpers or newer frontend APIs. Include cancellation and cleanup; do not create unbounded work behind a semaphore.
- Reuse repository tooling. uv, Ruff, ty, Asyncer, SQLModel and HTTPX are options, not mandatory migrations. Do not enable telemetry/exporters or start a production server as a side effect of editing an endpoint.

## Verify behavior

Use the configured targeted ASGI tests and local quality checks. Verify the changed public body/schema, invalid inputs, authorization, error status and resource cleanup as applicable. Exercise app lifespan when a test depends on its resources.

For streaming, distinguish producer iteration, in-process HTTP buffering and an actual incremental/disconnect test. Report which was observed; a buffered TestClient result does not prove deployed backpressure or proxy behavior. Inspect test setup before contacting services or modifying data. Do not install missing tooling merely to claim a check passed.

Use a defect/control comparison when it materially validates a regression claim; keep scratch inputs isolated. Report unrun tests, missing dependencies and unsupported version cells. Separate schema/type-check success from runtime behavior.

## Report

Return the implemented scope, version evidence, public behavior changes, files affected, actual tests/results and unverified behavior. Identify any dependency/configuration change and its side effects. Do not commit, publish, deploy or launch external services without the applicable authorization.
